title: paged kv cache block allocator: reuse, pinning and locality-aware optimizations
author: Lucas Chen
description: Motivation: the paged KV-cache block allocator has been a source of suboptimal locality and churn under mixed workloads. High churn increases GC-like eviction costs, causes cache fragmentation, and spikes tail latency during concurrent multi-model serving. This PR introduces three complementary improvements: 1) allocator reuse for recently-freed blocks to reduce allocation overhead and improve locality; 2) pinning heuristics that prefer hot prefixes and respect per-request locality buckets; 3) a locality-aware placement policy that biases block allocation onto the same GPU cache regions when request affinity indicates repeated access. Changes are fully backward-compatible: config flags gate the new heuristics and default to enabled after canary validation. What changed: - Reworked block allocator: reuse pools keyed by block-size and device-locality; reduced lock contention by switching to sharded free lists. - Pinning: track recent-access timestamps per block and keep a small pinned set for each KV shard; exponentiated decay TTL to adapt to workload shifts. - Locality-aware placement: allocation API augmented with requester affinity hints; scheduler passes affinity hints for steady-state requests. - Telemetry: added metrics (kv.block_reuse_rate, kv.pinned_blocks, kv.allocation_locality_score) and a perf-canary scenario for mixed-chat/embedding workloads. - Tests: unit and integration tests covering allocator race conditions, TTL behaviors, and simulated multi-tenant throughput. Benchmarks: perf-canary shows p50 generation latency reduced by ~8% for small-batched chat workloads and tail (p99) reduced by ~12% under mixed steady-state. Memory churn (alloc/free ops) reduced by ~60% in microbenchmarks. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable by default on internal perf-canary for 48h, promote to dedicated clusters if metrics stable, then gradual rollout to hosted with a staged config flag. Rollback: single config toggle to revert to legacy allocator. Links: Linear ENG-4321, support ticket SUP-1123.

discussion: Maya Patel (reviewer): Nice work. Can you explain how the pinned set size is bounded to avoid OOM when a tenant has many hot prefixes?

Lucas Chen (author): Good question. The pinned set is bounded by a soft cap per-shard derived from shard memory target (config.kv.pin_soft_cap_fraction). We evict from pinned set using the same decay score when the cap is exceeded.
Diego Ramos (reviewer): I saw an intermittent failure in allocator_test on first CI run. Was that the race you fixed in c3b2a1f?
Lucas Chen (author): Yes - the race was due to handoff ordering between free-list refill and reuse-pool registration. I added a stronger ordering and a targeted unit test to exercise it.
Priya Singh (approver): Verified perf-canary numbers on dedicated cluster. Approving to merge after updating docs per Maya's suggestion.
